text:
Marcus Pettersson came to New York with a reputation as a quiet, defense-first partner, and Evolving-Hockey's numbers last season backed that up: opponents got fewer expected goals with him on than with almost any other defenseman, 98th percentile. He did it in Vancouver with some of the weakest teammates in the league.

The first 23 games as a Ranger have been fine without being dominant. He's at 21 minutes a night, five assists, no goals. New York gets about half the expected goals with him on at five on five, a little worse than without him. His pair with Sean Durzi had been underwater before Durzi got hurt (44% of the expected goals), and the two were reunited against Carolina on Nov 22.

His skating is the limitation: NHL Edge puts his top speed and acceleration near the bottom of the league. Evolving-Hockey's defensive numbers say it hasn't held him back much.

What to watch: whether the second pair can win its minutes with Durzi back. That's one of the Rangers' biggest questions, with Igor Shesterkin out for the season and less margin in net.
